Orrevall et al. studied patients with advanced cancer who had
received home parenteral nutrition (HPN) and found that the
desperate and chaotic situation in the family inﬂ uenced a pa-
tient’s willingness to accept HPN.81 It is unknown whether HPN 
can improve a patient’s quality of life. Quality of life is very 
diﬃ  cult to measure, and few studies have documented quality 
of life in advanced cancer patients who are on HPN. Bozzetti 
et al. studied patients with advanced cancer who received HPN 
with respect to nutritional status, length of survival, and quality 
of life. Th eir study suggests that in malnourished, chronically 
obstructed patients with advanced cancer resistant to conven-
tional curative therapy, HPN may help to prolong survival past 
seven months (in approximately one-third of patients), improve
their quality of life (in 20% to 40% of them), or at least maintain
it until two months prior to death.82
